database_summary: This SQLite database models metadata and results for machine-learning problems/datasets. The central entity is a 'problem' (dataset) identified by name. Other tables hold descriptive attributes of features (eda), feature-level and model-level importance metrics, model scores, declared models, and solution-level summaries. Many tables are versioned and stepped indicating repeated runs or pipeline stages. Most tables are histories/events (measurements per run) rather than a single current-state row per problem.

accepted.name: problem_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  path,
  type,
  target
FROM problem
accepted.description: Normalized canonical projection of the problem table. Use this when queries need stable problem-level attributes (one row per dataset name) for joins or filtering. | Use for: List datasets with their type and target; Join dataset metadata to scores or feature information; Filter problems by type or target

accepted.name: eda_features
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  version,
  feature,
  type,
  range,
  drop_user,
  drop_correlation,
  target
FROM eda
accepted.description: One row per (name, version, feature) describing EDA metadata for that feature and pipeline version. Use when analyzing feature-level flags (drop_user/drop_correlation) or types and ranges across versions. | Use for: Which features were dropped by user or due to correlation for a given problem/version; Aggregate feature types or ranges per dataset or version; Join feature-level metadata to feature importance

accepted.name: feature_importance_rollup
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  version,
  feature,
  AVG(importance) AS importance_mean,
  MAX(importance) AS importance_max,
  COUNT(*) AS importance_count
FROM feature_importance
GROUP BY name, version, feature
accepted.description: Aggregated feature importance per (name, version, feature) preserving step-level info by exposing mean and max importance across steps. Useful for ranking features across steps or comparing summary importance across versions. | Use for: Which features are most important on average for a dataset/version; Compare top features across versions; Filter features by aggregated importance

accepted.name: model_score_per_model
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  version,
  step,
  model,
  train_score,
  test_score
FROM model_score
accepted.description: One row per (name, version, step, model) with train and test scores. Use as the canonical model performance table for downstream joins and aggregations. | Use for: Compare train vs test performance per model; Choose best model per version/step; Compute model-level aggregates (mean test_score) across steps

accepted.name: best_model_rank_per_version
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  version,
  step,
  model,
  train_score,
  test_score,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY name, version ORDER BY test_score DESC) AS model_test_rank
FROM model_score
accepted.description: Ranks models within each (name, version) by test_score descending (best test first) and exposes rank and best_test_score. Use to select top-N models per dataset/version downstream by filtering on rank. | Use for: Select top-k models per dataset/version by test_score; Identify rank of a given model within its version; Aggregate metrics for top-ranked models

accepted.name: solution_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  version,
  correlation,
  nb_model,
  nb_feature,
  score,
  test_size,
  resampling
FROM solution
accepted.description: One row per (name, version) representing solution metadata and scores. Use as the canonical solution-level table for joins to problems and model-level results. | Use for: Compare solution scores across versions; Join solution metadata to model scores for analysis; Filter solutions by resampling or test_size

accepted.name: model_importance_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  version,
  model,
  AVG(importance) AS importance_mean,
  MAX(importance) AS importance_max,
  COUNT(*) AS importance_count
FROM model_importance
GROUP BY name, version, model
accepted.description: Aggregated model importance per (name, version, model) summarizing importance across steps (mean, max, count). Useful for comparing model-level importance stability across steps/versions. | Use for: Which models have highest average importance for a dataset/version; Stability of model importance across steps; Join to solution or model_score to explain performance

accepted.name: latest_version_per_problem
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  version,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY name ORDER BY version DESC) AS version_rank
FROM solution
accepted.description: Identifies the latest version per problem (name) by maximum version value and exposes a version_rank so downstream queries can filter for the latest release per dataset without hardcoding a literal. | Use for: Join other tables to the latest solution version per problem; Filter analyses to only the most recent version of each dataset

accepted.name: problem_with_latest_solution
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.name,
  p.path,
  p.type,
  p.target,
  s.version,
  s.correlation,
  s.nb_model,
  s.nb_feature,
  s.score,
  s.test_size,
  s.resampling
FROM problem p
JOIN solution s ON p.name = s.name
JOIN (
  SELECT name, MAX(version) AS max_version FROM solution GROUP BY name
) sv ON s.name = sv.name AND s.version = sv.max_version
accepted.description: Denormalized view joining problem metadata to its latest solution version (as defined by the highest solution.version). Use when evaluating problem-level metrics using the most recent solution without specifying a version literal. | Use for: Show each dataset with its most recent solution and score; Compare problem metadata to latest solution attributes; Seed further joins using the latest version per problem
